title: pH of weak acids/bases; salt hydrolysis; pH curves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB06#t2 term and clue written for the game; AB07#t2 term and clue written for the game; AB06#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB06#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB06#N.3a, AB07#N.4a, AB06#N.4, AB07#N.13, AB06#N.15b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ka
items.clue: Equals [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA] for the equilibrium HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻.

items.label: Buffer region
items.clue: Gentle slope before the steep section, where HA and A⁻ are both present.

items.label: Hydrolysis
items.clue: The reaction of an ion with water, as when CH₃COO⁻ takes H⁺ and leaves OH⁻.

items.label: Kb
items.clue: Equilibrium constant for a weak base reacting with water: B + H₂O ⇌ BH⁺ + OH⁻.

questions.stem: What is the pH of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH(aq), at 298 K? Ka = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵. Assume that the equilibrium concentration of CH₃COOH equals its initial concentration.
25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid (pKa = 4.76) is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) at 298 K. What is the pH after 12.5 cm³ of NaOH(aq) has been added?
questions.explanation: 12.5 cm³ is half the equivalence volume. Half the CH₃COOH is now CH₃COO⁻, so [CH₃COOH] = [CH₃COO⁻], [H⁺] = Ka and pH = pKa = 4.76.

questions.stem: A 0.20 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak acid, HA, has pH 2.70 at 298 K. What is Ka?

Separate 20.0 cm³ portions of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) and of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ base B(aq) are each titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq). Both need 20.0 cm³ of acid. Which feature of the curves shows that B is a weak base?

options.text: B's curve needs a larger volume of acid to reach its equivalence point than the NaOH curve does.
B's curve starts at a lower pH, falls gently at first, and reaches equivalence below pH 7.
B's curve has no steep section at all, because a weak base reacts with the acid only partly.
B's curve reaches its equivalence point above pH 7, because B is a base and so stays alkaline.

questions.stem: Propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH, is a weak acid used to stop bread going mouldy. What is the pH of 0.050 mol dm⁻³ propanoic acid at 298 K? pKa = 4.87.
